textoCompleto:
Wood-Downes Scale

RESPIRATORY DISTRESS ASSESSMENT

Assess and quantify the severity of respiratory failure in newborns to guide interventions in the Neonatal ICU.
Patient Data

Fill out for the Medical Record/PDF Report

Clinical Parameters
Auscultation of respiratory wheezes.

Use of accessory muscles.

Assessment of air entry into the lungs.

Bluish discoloration of skin/mucous membranes.

Breaths per minute (breaths/min).

Beats per minute (bpm).

Final Wood-Downes Score

Assessment Memory

Suggested NANDA Diagnoses
Based on the assessment of distress and ventilatory stability.

Processing clinical reasoning...

Frequently Asked Questions
Follow more nursing information on our Nursing Forum.

Related Scales
Silverman-Anderson Respiratory distress assessment.

Apgar Scale Newborn vitality.

CRIES Scale Neonatal/pediatric pain assessment

Scientific Reference
MARTINS, T. B. Assessment of respiratory distress in children with acute viral bronchiolitis: an integrative review. Undergraduate Thesis, Santa Catarina State University (UDESC), Florianópolis, SC, 2019. Online access .

Score Interpretation

No Distress (0)
Newborn in good respiratory condition. Routine care.

Mild Distress (1 to 3 points)
Initial signs of respiratory distress. Requires continuous monitoring and possible mild support.

Moderate Distress (4 to 7 points)
Compromised respiratory status. Clinical intervention required for stabilization.

Severe Distress (8 to 14 points)
Respiratory failure. Assess need for advanced ventilatory support and ICU admission.
